column1: # Feed registry — the sources this project watches for NEW information.
# One row per feed. Columns are TAB separated:
#   key              stable short name, used in state and reports
#   url              the feed URL
#   cap              what it can tell us: OBJ ORG MONEY EVENT TECH POLICY
#   cadence_minutes  how often the PUBLISHER says it updates, 0 = unstated
#   verified         yes|no — has this URL been fetched and parsed BY US
#   verified_on      ISO date of that measurement, or blank
#   basis            why this feed is in the list. >40 chars. A reviewer
#                    must be able to act on it without asking anyone.
# RULE, and the reason this file ships mostly unverified:
# a feed URL recalled from memory is a guess (AD-112 — there is no SIC
# 3761). Every row below that says verified=no has NOT been fetched by
# this project. `python -m src.feeds.watch --verify` fetches each one
# from YOUR network, records what actually came back, and rewrites the
# verified/verified_on columns. Until then the rows are candidates, not
# sources, and --poll skips them unless given --include-unverified.
# The four SEC rows were measured through the session's fetcher on
# 2026-10-13 and are marked verified=no ANYWAY, because that fetcher is
# not the network the pipeline runs on and two of the three XBRL feeds
# came back months stale. Re-measure locally. See the staleness note in
# docs/API_USAGE_POLICY.md.
key
sec_press
column7: SEC press releases. Enforcement and rule changes that move a filer's disclosure obligations, which is upstream of every number sec_edgar.py reads.

column1: sec_litigation
column7: SEC litigation releases. A filer under enforcement is a filer whose reported figures may be restated; a restatement is a competing claim, not a correction.

column1: sec_xbrl_usgaap
column7: Up to 200 latest filings with US-GAAP or IFRS tagged financial statements, carrying edgar:cikNumber and edgar:assignedSic. The arrival signal for sec_edgar.py — tells us a NEW 10-K exists without polling 16 filers.

column1: sec_xbrl_all
column7: All XBRL filings, up to 200. Broader than the US-GAAP feed and the cheapest way to notice a space filer we have not seeded, because every item carries its SIC.

column1: nasa_news
column7: NASA news releases. Mission milestones, award announcements and programme changes — the EVENT cap, and one of the news sources the cost model is meant to build inferences from.

column1: nasa_technology
column7: NASA technology news. Directly adjacent to the TechPort TRL data already ingested; a TRL change is usually announced here before TechPort's record moves.

column1: nasa_jpl
column7: JPL centre news. Highest spacecraft-per-release rate of any NASA centre feed, which is what makes it worth a row of its own rather than relying on the firehose.

column1: nasa_all
column7: NASA recently-published content, all of it. Listed as the fallback if the topical feeds prove too narrow; expected to be noisy enough that it stays off by default.

column1: fed_register_sec
column7: Federal Register, SEC agency id 466 — the URL pattern is the SEC's own, taken from sec.gov/about/rss-feeds. Proves the conditions[agency_ids][] parameter works, so FCC and NOAA rows can be added the same way once their ids are READ rather than guessed.
